source_text: OK; before we started on this big Minard campaign, what we were talking about was aligning operator turns, patterns, PBASE levels, and R-numbers so that we can make a model of the operator in AIF terms.  I'm noticing one problem here which is that turns-patterns-PBASE works reasonably well but the link PBASE-to-R-numbers is a one-to-many and we don't have a signal to derive that yet.  The only thing that might work could be to make a direct patterns-to-R-numbers alignment.  Possibly this is something that we have tried already.

reply_text:
I'm checking whether the pattern-stage label files already carry R-nodes, and how the intent table assigns them.The label file already has a `:node` field per pattern. Checking how many are filled:㊥ (patterns to R-numbers: tried already?) Yes, partly. The pattern-stage label files already have an optional R-node field per pattern, but only 66 of the 786 labelled patterns have one: 231 of the 3,035 hits in that file, about 8%. Most of those 66 are patterns that are about a War Machine component, not patterns where you are doing that step yourself. So the direct alignment we have is sparse, and it mostly records the topic. It doesn't yet give a signal for which R-node a turn lands on.

㊢ (what's in the existing labels) The field is `:node` in `futon0/analysis/audits/pattern-stages-2026-10-01.edn`, filled during the same hand coding that set the stages.
- **TRACE:** has the most, 25 patterns and 99 hits, nearly all assurance practices such as changelog-trail and term-to-channel-traceability.
- **Loop R-nodes:** most have one to five patterns, and most of those are the `problems/rN-…` and `aif/…` entries describing the component itself. Examples are `problems/r10-scheduled-entrypoint` and `aif/interoceptive-tripwires`.
- **Topical vs functional:** 38 of the 66 are topical subject patterns, against 27 that are functional practices.
- **Coverage:** R12, R13 and R11 have one hit each. R19, R3a, CTAU and GRAIN-GATE have none.

So a turn that retrieves `problems/r14-commitment-temperature` is a turn about R14. It isn't evidence that you were setting commitment temperature yourself.

🈖 (where the one-to-many lives) The stages split as follows in `p4ng/empirics-futon/control-stages.edn`:
- **PERCEIVE:** R2, R8, R19
- **BELIEVE:** R1, R3, R3a, R7
- **EVALUATE:** R4, R5, plus the two CTAU nodes
- **SELECT:** R6, R13, R14, R15, R11, plus GRAIN-GATE
- **ACT:** R16 only

The assurance row adds R10, R12, R20, R17 and R9. So ACT already maps to one node, and the ambiguity is mainly in SELECT and BELIEVE.

㊭ (a second signal we already have) The intent table in `futon3/src-cljs/futon3/turnfeed/core.cljs` assigns each 象 intent an R-node. That assignment is claude-12's untested proposal from 25 September. It is independent of the patterns: patterns come from what a turn retrieves, intents from how the annotator reads your wording. Where a turn has both and they agree on the stage, the intent could pick the R-node within the stage. One example would be a SELECT pattern plus a "prioritize" intent. I'd start with a cross-tabulation, before relabelling any patterns:
1. Take turns with a stage from their pattern and an intent from 象.
2. Count how often the two agree on the stage.
3. Within agreeing turns, see how evenly the intent's R-nodes spread.

If they agree often and the intents spread across several R-nodes, that's a usable signal. If not, the remaining option is the direct relabelling you describe. I'd restrict that to functional patterns (what the THEN clause has you do), assign R-nodes only within the pattern's stage, and allow "none" where no R-node fits.

🈸 (go-ahead) Shall I run that cross-tabulation? It reads existing records only, so it's a small job I can do here.

previous_reply_acts.text: (how it will be checked) Kimi has to write a Playwright check that loads the page in headless Chromium and fails on any script error. That is how the `tokenDataEnd` error got through last time. For each of the eight stages, the check opens it by click and by keyboard, and confirms the number of family bands drawn matches the data. It also checks the back button, hover values, and light and dark themes. The 09-21 page must stay byte-identical. Kimi won't publish; when it reports back, I'll break one stage on purpose to see that the check catches it, run the check myself, look at the screenshots, then publish and give you the URL.
